Chapter 10: Sustaining Change and Embracing Lifelong Growth
You know, the journey toward healthier relationships and a stronger sense of self isn’t something you just check off a list. It’s ongoing—full of twists, turns, and sometimes, old patterns popping back up. Especially when life gets stressful, or you find yourself in new situations, it’s so easy to slip into those familiar habits. But here’s the thing: it’s not about being perfect. What really matters is persistence—a gentle, steady return to awareness and choice, again and again.
So, how do you actually sustain change over time? Let’s look at a few ways.
First, take a moment for regular self-reflection. You might ask yourself, “Which ego state is guiding me right now?” Just checking in like this helps you stay present and make conscious choices.
Next, keep practicing Adult-to-Adult communication, even if it feels a bit awkward at first. It’s like learning a new language—the more you use it, the more natural it becomes.
And don’t be afraid to reach out for support when you need it. That could mean talking to a friend, seeking advice from a mentor, or even connecting with a professional who can help you navigate challenges.
Think of growth as a spiral, not a straight line. Each time you loop around, you gain new insights, and you get another shot at deepening your understanding. Setbacks? They’re not failures. They’re actually invitations to revisit and strengthen your foundation.
Along the way, keep these gentle reminders close:
Be patient—with yourself and with others. Real change takes time and courage.
Celebrate your progress, no matter how small it seems. Every step forward matters.
And always remember, everyone’s carrying their own history and struggles. So, a little compassion goes a long way.
Ultimately, the goal isn’t to get rid of your Parent or Child parts. Instead, it’s about bringing all those pieces together. Your Adult self can become a wise, compassionate guide, drawing strength from every part of who you are.
As this integration deepens, you’ll notice your relationships becoming more authentic, more resilient, and yes—more joyful. The “I’m OK – You’re OK” mindset isn’t some finish line to cross. It’s a way of being—one you can choose, moment by moment, every single day.
